messages.subject: multicore option for fitting a model in lavaan
parts:
dear users,

is there an easy option to use multiple cores for fitting a model in lavaan?
i've tried to write a function using mclapply around it (as a laywoman :-S), but am experiencing a couple of problems ... 

-----
analyzemodel <- function (model, data) {
 fit <- sem(model=model1, data=data, estimator="MLR", missing="fiml", se="robust", std.lv=T)
 summarymodel <- summary(fit, fit.measures=T, standardized=T, rsquare=T)
}

model1 <- '
........
'
output <- mclapply(data, analyzemodel)
-----

i only get the error that all cores reported errors in the user's code, i guess one problem is that i am using 'data', which is a data matrix, as object for the mclapply function... any ideas which object i should define there?

sorry for the stupid question... your help is much appreciated! thank you very much!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: multicore option for fitting a model in lavaan
parts:
What independent task do you expect each core to perform?  ML estimation is an iterative process that requires knowledge of the previous iteration to know how to iterate forward, so that task cannot be farmed out to independent processes that don't communicate with each other.

If you were fitting this model to a series of data sets (e.g., in a simulation or multiple imputations), you could use the parallel options in the lavaanList() function.  If you were bootstrapping, the bootstrapLavaan() function has parallel options (same situation: the model is fit independently to a bunch of different data sets, so that can be done on different cores).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

It's old post, but I can answer differently to your question.

You can always use Microsoft R Open, it's an overlay for R from Microsoft. 

I don't know about differencies to simple R, but Microsoft R can do calculations on all of the cores at once. It's not doing few task like one task at one core, but doing one task on all of the cores of PC.
